findings.summary: The colon-switch bullets are the second block on the page, before any default operator has been shown, and they duplicate section 3 further down the same page.
findings.evidence: Page 5 block 2: "No colon = only UNSET triggers the default." / "An empty variable stays empty." / "Same switch applies across all these operators." — placed before heading "1. Braces Disambiguate", before the "2. Default Operators" table introduces `${v:-d}`, and duplicating "3. The Colon Switch" (table rows unset/empty/`x`).
findings.fix: Delete this stray bullet group from the top of page 5 and keep the content only under "3. The Colon Switch", where the `${v:-d}` vs `${v-d}` table gives it a referent.

findings.summary: ANSI-C quoting and double-quote concatenation are used in a page-1 code block but are only defined on page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 1 code: "\"$HOME\"/bin/'my app'   # ONE word" / "$'\\t'                  # a real tab" / "$'\\x41' $'\\u00e9'      # A and e-acute", while page 2 heading "2. Dollar-Quoting" first states "`$'...'` is ANSI-C quoting" and heading "1. Double Quotes" first states the double-quote rules.
findings.fix: Move that code block to page 2, immediately after the "2. Dollar-Quoting" bullets, so the `$'...'` and adjacent-concatenation rules are stated before they are demonstrated.

findings.summary: A `read`/IFS idiom closes the single-quotes section, using three constructs that are not defined until page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 1 final block: "IFS=: read -r a b c <<< \"$line\"" / "# prefix applies to this read only", whereas page 3 introduces "`IFS` = Internal Field Separator" and "`-r` is mandatory: keeps backslashes intact."
findings.fix: Move this block to page 3 under "3. Reading Lines", after the `while IFS= read -r line` loop and the `-r` bullets.

findings.summary: The quoting chapter teaches single quotes and backslash before double quotes, and its section numbers run 6, 7, 1, 2, 3.
findings.evidence: Page 1 heading "6. Single Quotes"; page 2 headings in order: "7. Backslash & Joining", then "1. Double Quotes", "2. Dollar-Quoting", "3. No Nesting" — yet double quotes are already used on page 1 ("\"$HOME\"/bin/'my app'") and in the page-1 `IFS=: read ... <<< \"$line\"` example.
findings.fix: Reorder the chapter to Double Quotes → Single Quotes → Backslash & Joining → Dollar-Quoting → No Nesting and renumber the headings 1–5 so the sequence is continuous.

findings.summary: A trailing code block on page 2 explains itself by contrast with word splitting, which is not introduced until page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 2 final block: "echo a   b        # prints: a b" / "# parser collapsed the spaces as tokens" / "# different mechanism from word splitting" — page 3's "4. What Actually Splits" is the first definition of word splitting.
findings.fix: Move this block to page 3 immediately after the "4. What Actually Splits" bullets, where the contrast has both terms available.

findings.summary: The three-cell comparison row under "4. Splitting On Purpose" has its last cell rendered outside the table frame, unbordered and running into the right margin.
findings.evidence: Cells "$x: zero args" and "\"$x\": one empty arg" are boxed, but the third cell "x=\"\" then f $x vs f \"$x\"" has no borders and its text extends past the table's right edge to the page margin.
findings.fix: Give the table a fixed three-column width that fits the column area and let the third cell wrap inside its border, or shorten the cell text to "x=''; f $x vs f \"$x\"".

findings.summary: The page ends with glob claims that depend on the glob operator table on page 4.
findings.evidence: Page 3 final bullets: "`*` also matches the empty string." / "Globs are NOT regexes." / "Glob `*` = any characters; regex `*` = repeat previous atom." — page 4's "5. The Operators" table is the first place `*` is defined as "any string, never `/`".
findings.fix: Move these three bullets to page 4 directly after the operators table, where `*` has just been defined.

findings.summary: In the "3. The Shell Expands, Not ls" flow diagram, the connector lines are drawn straight through the box labels so the words read as struck out.
findings.evidence: A horizontal connector runs through the middle of the "matches names" and "builds argv" boxes, crossing the glyphs of both labels; the same happens on the "sees a b c" / "never sees *" row below.
findings.fix: Route diagram edges to box perimeters (anchor arrows on the node borders and add node padding) instead of drawing node-centre-to-node-centre lines over the label text.

findings.summary: An indirect-expansion example runs a page before indirect expansion is defined.
findings.evidence: Page 5 code: "for n in \"${!APP_@}\"; do" / "  printf '%s=%s\\n' \"$n\" \"${!n}\"" — page 6 "4. Length & Indirection" first says "`${!var}` is indirect: var='HOME' yields `$HOME`" and "`${!prefix*}` and `${!prefix@}` list names by prefix."
findings.fix: Move the enumeration loop to page 6, immediately below the "4. Length & Indirection" bullets.

findings.summary: Three bullets on page 5 have no antecedent — they describe the fork-free path surgery that is not introduced until page 6.
findings.evidence: Page 5 bullets: "Safe with newlines in filenames." / "No fork means no process-creation cost." / "A loop of `basename` pays milliseconds per iteration." — the subject, "${path##*/}    # basename, no fork", first appears on page 6 under "2. Path Surgery".
findings.fix: Move these bullets to page 6 directly after the "2. Path Surgery" code block (or merge them into page 7's "Zero Forks" callout).

findings.summary: Bullets about case modification and the `@` transforms appear a page before the table that defines them, and the chapter's sections run 1, 2, 3, 5, then 4.
findings.evidence: Page 6 bullets: "Case modification needs Bash 4+." / "`${v@Q}` is the correct way to build a string for `eval` or `ssh`." / "`${v@A}` emits a reusable declaration." — the defining table, heading "4. Case And @ Transforms" with rows "`${v^}` `${v^^}`" and "`${v@Q}`", sits on page 7 after page 6's "5. Element-Wise On Arrays".
findings.fix: Move section 4 ("Case And @ Transforms" table) and these bullets onto page 6 ahead of "5. Element-Wise On Arrays", keeping the bullets below the table.

findings.summary: The handbook presents `> $file` as producing an "ambiguous redirect", but bash only errors when the redirection word expands to zero or more than one word.
findings.evidence: Page 1 code block: "> $file    # unquoted: ambiguous redirect"; page 9 bullet: "Unquoted redirection: 'ambiguous redirect' error."
findings.fix: Change the comment to "> $file   # ambiguous redirect ONLY if $file is empty or splits into several words" and reword the page-9 bullet to "Unquoted redirection target: 'ambiguous redirect' when it expands to zero or multiple words — quote it anyway."

findings.summary: `!` is listed as a character that stays "live" inside double quotes, but history expansion is off in non-interactive shells, so `!` is literal in scripts — and `\!` there leaves a stray backslash.
findings.evidence: Page 2 bullet: "Live characters: `$`, backtick, `\`, and `!`." followed by "Backslash escapes only `$` ` \" \\ and newline."
findings.fix: Qualify it: "Live characters: `$`, backtick, `\` — plus `!` in interactive shells only (history expansion is disabled in scripts, and `"\!"` leaves the backslash; use `"..."'!'` if you must)".

findings.summary: The expansion-pipeline debugging block is stranded under the backslash section, a page away from the pipeline it debugs.
findings.evidence: Page 2, directly under "7. Backslash & Joining": "set -x                    # trace after expansion" / "printf '[%s]\\n' $var      # count the arguments" — the pipeline and its "Memorise One Sentence" callout are on page 1.
findings.fix: Move this block to page 1, immediately after the "Memorise One Sentence" callout, so the debug tool closes the pipeline section.

findings.summary: A tiny red "Ans" label under the "Why is for x in $(cat file) a bug?" heading is rendered at an unreadably small size.
findings.evidence: Between the heading "Why is for x in $(cat file) a bug?" and the bullet "It splits on every whitespace run." sits a ~6px red underlined token that cannot be resolved as text at page scale.
findings.fix: Render the answer label at the normal body font size (or drop it) rather than inheriting a shrunken caption style.

findings.summary: The Default Operators table describes `${v:+alt}` as firing when the variable is "set", omitting that the colon form also requires it to be non-empty.
findings.evidence: Table row: ["`${v:+alt}`","alt only if set"] — while the sibling row correctly reads ["`${v:-d}`","d if unset or empty"].
findings.fix: Change the cell to "alt if set AND non-empty" (reserve "alt only if set" for the colon-less `${v+alt}`).

findings.summary: The arrays chapter contains two sections numbered 1, so the second reads as the start of a new chapter.
findings.evidence: Page 7 headings: "1. Declare And Index", "2. [@] Versus [*]", "3. Count, Indices, Append", then "1. Loading From Files"; page 8 continues with "4. Associative Arrays".
findings.fix: Renumber "Loading From Files" to 4 and "Associative Arrays" to 5.

findings.summary: Bullets about `[[ ... ]]` are attached to the positional-slicing section, where they have no connection to the surrounding material.
findings.evidence: Page 8, after "5. Slicing Positionals" and its `\"${@:2}\"` code: "Prefer `[[ ... ]]` in Bash." / "No word splitting or globbing on operands." / "Quote RIGHT side of `==` unless globbing."
findings.fix: Move these bullets to page 9 beneath "2. Test Syntax", next to the `[ $x = y ]` examples they contrast with.

findings.summary: Two different sections on page 9 carry the number 6.
findings.evidence: Page 9 headings: "6. Legitimate `\"$*\"`" at the top and "6. Exit Status" near the bottom.
findings.fix: Renumber the carried-over `"$*"` section (e.g. to "$@ vs $*, cont.") or drop its number so the page has a single 1–6 sequence.
